reviews.title: Poor in Europe
reviews.text: It doesn’t seem to account for road width, so guides along very narrow slow lanes when a better road with a centre line is available.  In the US with wide roads this may not be an issue but it certainly is across Europe.

reviews.title: Stephen Hawking fans only
reviews.text: Awful experience. The idea is great but it’s very poor in navigation, re-routes and the voice navigation is a 90’s version of Stephen Hawking - I just can’t listen to it.  Deleting

reviews.title: When you pause a ride it does not return
reviews.text:
When you pause a ride you cannot in pause it. I had to remove the app and then reload it to unfreeze it! 
I and riding in Europe with a friend. We up loaded the same source GPX files and everyday the route on my app was different to my friends
Over 5 days of riding we have constantly been diverted in to urban developments  away from rural riding!! Do not use this app as it has not been fully developed

reviews.title: Just not as good as less costly options
reviews.text: I got a subscription as a deal with a CarPlay unit I bought. It wasn’t really worth the £5 I paid for it. Certainly not worth the full price. I don’t know how they do business, perhaps it’s through trapping buyers that buy it at a special rate into renewal without warning, and then refusing to stop the subscription, even if you stop it on the same day as it renews. Crooks. Avoid like the plague. If the app was any good they would need to use these tactics. Despite saying I can contact them, they still create a subscription trap.  Hollow words!

reviews.title: Mediocre at best
reviews.text: Some of the route planning functionality is handy, but can be a bit hit and miss route wise. The navigation is poor and as a premium only option is expensive and poorly executed. Particularly unhelpful if you rely on the audio prompts only without a map display while riding. For example “continue straight ahead” or  “turn left” may be the same thing depending on road layout. Plan your routes yourself and stick with Google Maps for navigation.

reviews.title: Route generation poor
reviews.text: Takes you down bumpy narrow single track roads, regardless of what setting you apply. Tried this app a few times now and experimented with every option and it still takes you down poorly surfaced farm roads just because they look curvy on a map. How this yet to be fixed yet is beyond belief, I’ve tried it multiple times since release to same avail.

reviews.title: Useless app very buggy
reviews.text: Well had high hopes for this, subscribed to the app and went on holiday, the app was very buggy and consistently routed us incorrectly to find the nearest petrol station - it sent us 20 miles in the wrong direction when it had several garages within 1 mile of our location. Then upon me adding  all the photos of the trip within the app it crashes upon saving the end of the ride and now the app I locked up and calimoto cannot recover the ride or end it sucessfully. So have lost all the photos and after the first day of a 7 day adventure and nothing can be done other than delete the app and lose the photos. Won’t be using this again after the expirience. Will try a different app that does work I guess 🤷🏼‍♂️

reviews.title: Auto-Renewal
reviews.text: I used the App on a trip to Spain 2 years ago. I found it OK, nothing beyond that. I noted last week that the subscription had been auto-renewed. This despite no notification from Calimoto. They are refusing to refund the amount, despite the account and App not having been used in 14 months.

reviews.title: will sign you up regardless
reviews.text: had this app for 5 seconds bc i don’t pay for stuff like this when i can find an app that’s actually free. why do i wake up at 6am to an email that i have 9 days left on my subscription. i would NEVER pay for a subscription to an app. i’m looking everywhere to cancel it before they take my money & the only way i can get it to cancel is to delete my whole account (that’s fine i literally don’t use this and they’re trying to take my money) thing is i don’t even know if that worked & who knows if i’ll get charged regardless. even if you don’t want to use it they will try to take your money. do not download unless you want to go thru that horrendous hassle of trying to unsubscribe from a subscription you NEVER asked for!!!

reviews.title: You’re on your own
reviews.text: First, even the free trial makes you authorize payment prior to signing up. Considering they have no customer service access through the app or online, it is hard to trust that you can cancel prior to the deadline e if needed. Next you cannot set routes online, you need to do everything in the app so since there is little to no help available it is too time consuming to figure the app out on your own compared to other available apps

reviews.title: Great routes
reviews.text: Used for a couple of years now and really like the variety of routes and ability to keep away from motorway and busy A roads, occasionally puts u on a ‘track’ but otherwise 👍

reviews.title: Good app,
reviews.text:
I really enjoyed using Calimoto while it was included with my CHIGEE AIO-6 LTE purchase. Unfortunately, my experience with customer support has completely changed my opinion.

My subscription renewed automatically after one year, and I contacted support immediately after noticing the charge. I hadn’t intended to continue the subscription and requested a goodwill refund within days of the renewal.

Despite explaining the situation, and despite not intending to use the renewed subscription, my request was rejected with what appeared to be a standard copy-and-paste response.

The app itself is good and for the 12 month I used was great, but customer service and flexibility towards loyal users were very disappointing. I expected much better.

reviews.title: Not the adventure I want
reviews.text:
I’ve used Calimoto four times now, and every single ride has included at least one very long (we are talking miles) single-track lane. Today it really outdid itself by trying to send my cruiser down what looked more like an overgrown farm track than a road. I was half expecting to meet a herd of cows coming the other way!

The route planning idea is great, but if there was an option to avoid narrow single-track roads, it certainly didn’t seem to work for me. Until that improves, I can’t give it more than two stars.
Update: I did try the fast “Fast” routing setting and that was the day it tried to send me down a single road that was basically a farm track. I went out numerous times trying different setting but every time I took me down some single track lane where you have to pray there’s a passing point if you meet other traffic as being on a motorbike means reversing is extremely difficult.

reviews.title: Not good
reviews.text: Crashed my phone, very difficult to cancel subscription, overpriced. Avoid this app

reviews.title: disappointment
reviews.text: for how expensive the subscription is, this app should be the best app on my phone. not the case. half the time when you open the app, you get the spinning wheel of death. the other half of the time, you go to generate a ride and the button does literally nothing. like everything else in this world, the app was great when it came out and became junk over time. a shame really.

reviews.title: Dated; but has potential (and a bunch of issues I can’t get past)
reviews.text:
I’ve been riding for a couple of years and often go out with no destination in mind, so finding new routes can be a challenge. I discovered this app through a motorcycle Discord community and was immediately interested by the automatic round-trip generator, especially the option to prioritise twisty roads.

When I started planning my first ride, I found that the feature required a subscription. That wasn’t a problem for me, so I signed up for the free trial and headed out.

Unfortunately, less than 10 minutes into the ride, I’d already decided to cancel. A few issues stood out:

• The navigation voice sounds incredibly dated and robotic. It genuinely felt like using a GPS from the early 2000s.

• The speedometer is almost useless. Riders know motorcycle speedometers are often inaccurate, which is why I usually rely on Waze’s GPS speed reading. Calimoto includes a GPS speedometer, but it rounds to the nearest 5 mph, making it far less useful than it should be.

• The map refresh rate and navigation responsiveness are poor. I missed several turns because the map felt like it was lagging behind my actual position. Waze dynamically zooms in at lower speeds so junctions and exits are easy to see. Calimoto stays zoomed out, and by the time the map updates, you’ve often already passed the turn.

The route generation itself seemed promising, I would have probably only used it to generate round trips and still be happy to pay the subscription fee, but the navigation experience wasn’t

reviews.title: So far no good.
reviews.text: Not good with Apple CarPlay on my road glide, no sound was coming through for the directions and if the phone screen shut off, the ride would stop and even though no sound was coming through with navigation the. Every time directions came on the screen it would stop my music from playing. Not worth $80 a year if it doesn’t talk to me and integrate with apple CarPlay. My husband had similar issues on his Samsung as well were attempting to share a group ride.

reviews.title: Did not meet expectations
reviews.text:
I recently took a 5000 mile motorcycle trip from Alabama to Arizona and back. I considered several apps to use for planning this trip and settled on Calimoto. This app did an acceptable job of generally getting me from one point to another, but it is lacking in many ways.

The route that it would choose was not particularly "motorcycle friendly." It supposedly finds good motorcycle roads, but it often confuses curvy roads for good motorcycle roads. It would direct me around a town instead of through the town because the route around the town was more curvy. But the route still had traffic lights and intersections. All it really did is take me on a longer path, but not necessarily a motorcycle friendly or fun path. It would also direct me to roads that were closed. The app knew that these roads were closed because there was a symbol on the map that indicated they were closed. So why did it send me there?

The information it provided was often inaccurate. Specifically, the speed limits were almost never accurate. It would be better if it did not show speed limits at all. And locations of services such as gas stations were not accurate. I spent a lot of time in west Texas where gas stations and service are sparse. The app identified several gas stations that turned out to be closed or non-existent. This is a big deal in places like west Texas when you really need to find a gas station.

There were a few instances when I had to drive through big cities. The app does not do a good

reviews.title: Beware
reviews.text: Everyone knows that what an automatic annual subscription means. Except that should you be reminded by a charge and you immediately contact support to cancel and get a refund (a courtesy) and they told you can’t, to me, that sounds like extremely poor customer service.

reviews.title: Hard to navigate
reviews.text: Was hoping this would be a good alternative but for the price I’ll stick with Google Maps.. if it was simpler to set up a round trip it would be good but is kind of janky to plan a trip on the app.

reviews.title: Not suitable for UK roads
reviews.text: Might be okay in Cali, but it’s bordering on dangerous on the UK roads. Avoid at all costs

reviews.title: Questionable routing quality
reviews.text:
I have just started using this app. My 2 main issues with it are:

1. It doesn’t always include junctions in routes where the rider does not have priority. I’ve come across this twice now. The first time was a crossroad where there was a stop sign and I had to cross a main road. The second time was a junction where I had to turn left and give way to oncoming traffic. 

2. The twisty setting is ridiculous. It takes you down, what I would describe as cart tracks. If you are crossing a town or city it takes you via the most convoluted routes that are just a waste of time. 

Additionally, the speed indicator only works in increments of 5mph. This isn’t too bad if you’re riding on a national speed limit road, but in a 30mph zone this could quite easily result in a ticket when Calimoto indicates you are at the limit.

reviews.title: Based on what I could do
reviews.text: This review is completely based upon what I was able to do in the app. I downloaded the app took a look at it and was ready for a test run for my next ride. The day came and we plotted out a route using the app, mind you it is one we ride frequently but I wanted to see how the app performed. Once I got the way points in and we were ready to take off I hit the start route button and nothing. Well not nothing, exactly. It took me to the screen to sign up for an $80 subscription. I am sure there was like a X amount of days before you are charged thing, but how many people forget to cancel before that time. Then you are out $80 for app that may or may not be good. Well, I don’t do that. Want to limit my access at first, cool, but you could easily set it up where you get 2-3 rides to check it out and then require the subscription. I don’t even have a problem paying for a sub if the app is good and the money is used to maintain the app. What I am not going to do is give money to something I can’t even test first. So based on my user experience of saving $80 and bot being able to use the app at all, you get 1 star.

reviews.title: Dangerous!
reviews.text: Dangerous app! Missed numerous roundabouts on route and directions were NOT clear. For example ‘left turns’ when you can only turn left on the road - terrible app.
